paragraphs: Friend, look at how many things came at David in one chapter. A king's order, a spear, soldiers outside his house, and three teams of messengers. And not one of them got him. Saul had the crown, the army and the spear, and he still couldn't touch a man God was watching over. That's the lesson sitting right on top of this passage (1 Samuel 19:10, 18).

Now look at HOW David got out. A friend, Jonathan, spoke up for him when it cost something (1 Samuel 19:4-5). His wife, Michal, warned him and lowered him from a window (1 Samuel 19:11-12). Then he went to Samuel, the prophet, and told him all that Saul had done to him (1 Samuel 19:18). I think that's worth holding onto, baker. God's help doesn't always show up as a lightning bolt. Sometimes it shows up as a friend with a good plan and a window.

Then there's Saul. He swore an oath one minute and threw a spear the next (1 Samuel 19:6, 10). He sent men to seize David, and the Spirit of God stopped them, and then stopped Saul himself (1 Samuel 19:20-24). Some plans just can't win, and I'd rather be on the side that isn't fighting God. So if you're being chased by something bigger than you today, take heart. And stay tuned, because the story between David and Saul is not over.
